reference: The runnable contract case uses GNU Bash's documented type -t and help builtins: a compiled-in ns command is reported as a builtin, and help lookup succeeds. Its expected marker is fixed in the suite. Namespace, mount, ID-map, seccomp, LSM-transition, and cgroup operations are DEFERRED; each names an independent GNU/kernel oracle or a disposable VM/mock requirement. No candidate operation output is used as an oracle.
coverage: Static builtin registration and help availability through Bash metadata builtins.
Deferred namespace creation and child execution semantics, including child exit propagation.
Deferred namespace-FD entry and user/group mapping behavior.
Deferred mount, pivot-root, and seccomp kernel effects in isolated disposable environments.
Deferred LSM transitions and cgroup v2 updates against controlled fixtures.
exclusions: No ns operation verb is invoked in this suite; namespace, mount, identity-map, security-policy, cgroup, and pivot-root effects need a purpose-built disposable VM or reviewed mock.
No live kernel, mount, LSM, cgroup, network, privilege, or host process behavior is claimed.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash reports ns as a statically available builtin and its documented help entry can be looked up. The marker is independent of the help text contents.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ns) == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help ns)
printf 'ns builtin; help available\n'

cases.purpose: Compare ns unshare for its supported namespace flags and the special for-children behavior of pid/time namespaces.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: The candidate's requested and unchanged namespace inodes are retained across the separate requests. Native setup succeeds, but comparable before/after native inode observations for all requested types were not retained. The original comparison remains incomplete; no extra all-six simultaneous invocation is required.; r2: No case.; r3: No case.; r5: The unprivileged UTS EPERM agrees with unshare; unsupported-namespace EINVAL was not exercised.

cases.purpose: Check clone-based namespace setup, argv/environment forwarding, PID namespace child semantics, --no-new-privs, and propagation of the child exit status.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r6: Exit 37 and missing-exec 127 are recorded; signal-to-128+S propagation was not exercised.

cases.purpose: Check setns using a descriptor for a controlled namespace, including ownership, invalid-descriptor, and permission behavior.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: No case.; r2: No case.; r4: The candidate and nsenter both receive EPERM on the saved descriptor; its owning initial user namespace is not independently established in the retained record.

cases.purpose: Check deny-setgroups ordering and uid_map/gid_map writes for a fresh user namespace.
Check private propagation, bind mounts, read-only bind remounts, and remount-readonly effects on fixture paths.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r2: No case.; r3: No case.; r4: No case.; r6: No case.

cases.purpose: Check the pivot-root syscall wrapper and resulting old-root placement using a disposable root tree.
Check loading and applying a binary sock_filter profile, including valid, malformed, and kernel-rejected profiles.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Candidate reports Seccomp 2 and an increased filter count, but individual before/after filter counts are not separately retained for independent comparison.; r6: Native control results are saved for the selected profiles, but candidate seccomp syscall outcomes are not independently traced for every profile.

cases.purpose: Check LSM detection and on-exec profile requests for AppArmor and SELinux, including unavailable and invalid-profile paths.
cases.reason: The detection and on-exec write paths are file-based and testable unprivileged with the documented root overrides; no fixture exists for them. A real AppArmor transition needs a test profile, and loading one needs CAP_MAC_ADMIN in the initial user namespace with an unload restore, which no driver provides. Missing capability: CAP_MAC_ADMIN in the initial user namespace. Writes to /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/.replace fail with EACCES/EPERM for uid 2000, and USERNS root has no MAC_ADMIN over the global policy. SELinux needs a different boot configuration and policy.

cases.purpose: Check cgroup v2 create, controller value, process membership, controller-enable, and remove behavior.
cases.reason: Writing cgroup files needs a writable delegated subtree. As uid 2000, mkdir under root-owned /sys/fs/cgroup returns EACCES; the legacy runner has no /sys. The root controller must create a per-side subtree and chown it to uid 2000 (cgroup delegation: directory, cgroup.procs, cgroup.subtree_control). The candidate hardcodes /sys/fs/cgroup (loadables/ns.c:532), so the fixture must address the subtree by its relative path from the root. Path validation needs no privilege.

cases.purpose: Bash help names the core namespace verbs; metadata only, with no syscall operation.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ns)
[[ $doc == *'ns unshare'* && $doc == *'ns spawn'* && $doc == *'ns enter'* ]]
printf 'namespace-verbs-documented\n'
